titulo: Brazilian Nun Is World’s Oldest Person at 116

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: LongeviQuest is an organization that keeps records of people over 110 years old around the world. It released a statement on Saturday saying that Canabarro is the world’s oldest person having proof of early life records.

LongeviQuest filmed a video of Canabarro last February. Canabarro can be seen smiling, making jokes and sharing small paintings she used to make of wildflowers. The video also shows her saying a Catholic prayer called the Hail Mary.
“I’m young, pretty and friendly — all very good, positive qualities that you have too,” the nun told visitors to her retirement home in the southern Brazilian city of Porto Alegre.
Cleber Canabarro is her 84-year-old nephew. He told The Associated Press that Sister Inah was so thin during childhood that many people worried that she would not live to be an adult.

Her nephew spends time with her every Saturday. He has been sending her voice messages between visits to help her feel better following two visits to the hospital that left her weak, with difficulty talking.
LongeviQuest researchers say Canabarro was born on June 8, 1908, to a large family in southern Brazil. But her nephew said her birth was registered two weeks late and she was actually born on May 27.

She started religious work when she was a teenager. She spent two years in Montevideo, Uruguay, before moving to Rio de Janeiro. She later settled in her home state of Rio Grande do Sul. Canabarro taught school for most of her life. One of her students was General João Figueiredo, a military leader and politician who served as the 30th president of Brazil from 1979 to 1985.

Pope Francis honored Canabarro for her 110th birthday. She is the second-oldest nun ever known, after Lucile Randon of France, who was the world’s oldest person until her death in 2023 at the age of 118.

The local soccer club where Canabarro lives is named Inter. The club celebrates the birthday of its oldest fan every year. Her room is decorated with gifts in the team’s red and white colors, her nephew said.

“White or black, rich or poor, whoever you are, Inter is the team of the people,” Canabarro said in one video posted on social media. The video shows her celebrating her 116th birthday with the club’s president.

LongeviQuest said Canabarro became the oldest living person following the death of Japan’s Tomiko Itooka in December. She now ranks as the 20th oldest documented person to have ever lived. The organization says Frenchwoman Jeanne Calment, who died in 1997 at the age of 122, was the oldest documented person ever.
titulo_es: Una monja brasileña, la persona más longeva del mundo a los 116 años
resumen_es: Perfil de la hermana Inah Canabarro, monja brasileña que a los 116 años se convirtió en la persona viva de más edad con documentación acreditada: su infancia, su vida como maestra y su pasión por el club de fútbol Internacional.
nivel_motivo: El texto es narrativo y de vocabulario cotidiano; el nivel léxico calculado sube por los nombres propios y algunos términos como «documented» o «nephew».

ideas_clave.idea: LongeviQuest, which tracks supercentenarians, has declared Canabarro the oldest living person with verified early-life records.
A video recorded the previous year shows her cheerful and humorous, displaying her flower paintings and praying.
Her nephew recalls that she was such a frail child that people feared she would not survive, and he now supports her after two hospital stays left her weak.
She was born into a large family in southern Brazil in 1908, although her nephew says her real birthday is earlier than the registered one.
She became a nun as a teenager and spent most of her life teaching, with a future Brazilian president among her pupils.
She was honoured by Pope Francis and is the second-oldest nun on record, after Frenchwoman Lucile Randon.
A devoted supporter of the local football club Inter, she celebrates her birthdays with the club, which she praises as a team for everyone.
She became the world's oldest person after the death of Japan's Tomiko Itooka and ranks twentieth among documented people ever, far behind Jeanne Calment.

resumen_modelo: The text reports that Inah Canabarro, a 116-year-old Brazilian nun, has been recognised by the research organisation LongeviQuest as the world's oldest living person, following the death of Tomiko Itooka of Japan. Although she was a sickly child, she has led a long and active life: she joined a religious order as a teenager, worked mainly as a teacher and even taught a future president of Brazil. Despite recent health problems, she remains cheerful and is a passionate supporter of the football club Inter, which celebrates her birthday every year. She is now the twentieth oldest documented person in history.
